title: Trump Claims Russia and Ukraine Agree to Halt Energy Strikes; Zelensky and Kremlin Voice Skepticism
detail: President Trump posted on Truth Social on September 14 that "Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy Targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!" — a day after telling Zelensky to stop striking Russian diesel infrastructure amid rising global fuel prices. Zelensky said he was "not sure" Russia would honor such a deal, offering conditional openness: Ukraine would halt strikes on Russian energy only "if the partners are ready to ensure Russia's real desire not to strike our electricity." An unnamed senior Ukrainian energy official told the Kyiv Independent they had received no notification of any energy ceasefire agreement. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Kyiv was not offering a "permanent settlement" aligned with Russian interests and was merely seeking a truce in Ukraine's "Achilles' heel," while separately describing Russian oil refineries as peaceful infrastructure. Zelensky said he plans to discuss an energy and Black Sea ceasefire with Trump at a possible meeting in New York September 21-23.

title: Russian Guided Aerial Bomb Strike on Izium Injures Three, Including 2-Month-Old Infant
detail: Russian forces struck the city of Izium in Kharkiv Oblast with a guided aerial bomb (KAB) at 08:01 on September 14, injuring a 56-year-old man, a 34-year-old woman, and their 2-month-old infant. The strike destroyed four private residential properties and damaged five private houses and parked vehicles, according to Kharkiv Regional Military Administration head Oleh Syniehubov. The strike came as Russian forces separately carried out 876 attacks on 54 settlements across Zaporizhzhia Oblast over the same 24-hour period.

title: NATO's Rutte, Poland's Tusk Pledge More Support for Ukraine After Border Drone Strike on Train
detail: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said on September 14 that the September 13 Russian drone strike near the Yahodyn-Dorohusk border crossing, which hit a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train roughly 2km from Poland, showed Vladimir Putin's "desperation and also his desire to sow fear and terror," and pledged increased military support for Ukraine along with strengthened NATO defenses on its eastern flank. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that Russia appears prepared to intensify operations near Ukraine's borders with European nations, saying "these coming weeks and months will be a time of very intensified actions on the Russian side." Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz separately reported recovering a suspected Russian military drone from the Baltic Sea.
